jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Conflict Navigation
jokes.joke: My wife gave me an ultimatum in a parking garage: “Ask someone where we parked or I’m walking home.” I said, “Go ahead.” She stormed off, hit the panic button, and our car started screaming two rows over. I don’t need directions; I need conflict.

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Level 4, Section C
jokes.joke: My wife gave me an ultimatum: find the car in ten minutes or we're getting divorced. So I did what any explorer would do — I picked a direction and committed. Twenty minutes later I'm sweating, circling Level 4 like Magellan, and she goes, 'That's it, we're done.' I said, 'Fine, but you're taking the bus.'

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Level 4B
jokes.joke: I lost my car in a six-story concrete parking garage yesterday, and after forty-five minutes of wandering, I stopped looking for my Honda Civic and started exploring uncharted territory like an 18th-century cartographer. I was claiming support pillars for the Spanish Crown and eating half an old granola bar from my pocket just to survive the harsh winter of Level 4B.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Garage Magellan
jokes.joke: I like to think of myself as an explorer. Last weekend I took on the ultimate challenge: finding a parking spot in a downtown garage. After circling for an hour I finally claimed a space on the lowest level. I felt like Magellan—except Magellan didn’t have to pay twenty bucks to exit.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Garage Ultimatum
jokes.joke: I knew I’d taken the whole ‘explorer’ thing too far when my partner gave me an ultimatum in a parking garage. I’m wandering around like I’m mapping uncharted territory, and they’re yelling, “Either find the car or find a new ride home.” I said, “I’m close—I’ve discovered three exits and a suspicious puddle.”

scores.comment: Clear escalation and a decent final reversal, but the explorer/Magellan material introduces a third seed concept and the divorce premise feels mechanically exaggerated.

Strong sustained analogy with specific images and good escalation. The Spanish Crown and survival details give it more texture than a standard lost-car bit, though the ending is more amusing than sharply punchy.
Clean and understandable, but the Magellan comparison and expensive-parking payoff are both predictable. Competent filler rather than a memorable turn.
The suspicious-puddle tag has some comic specificity, but the joke uses parking garage, explorer, and ultimatum concepts, exceeding the required two. The structure is solid but familiar.
Good escalation, panic-button reveal lands well, sharp closing line.
Premise is familiar and overstuffed with imagery; punchline is weak, more listing than landing.
Clean setup, Magellan tag is a nice concrete final beat though somewhat expected route.
Solid form but punchline (puddle/exits) is mild and doesn't fully snap.
Tightly constructed with a sharp twist on the ultimatum trope and a punchy closing line.
Accidentally leans on three seed concepts (ultimatum, parking garage, explorer), diluting prompt fit, and ends on a predictable relationship beat.
Very familiar premise and structure; the final comparison lands as mild observational filler.
Incorporates three seeds conceptually (explorer, ultimatum, parking garage) and finishes with a slightly soft list-of-observations punchline.
Solid premise and clean close on conflict preference; panic-button turn is familiar but lands.
Three seed concepts; Magellan bit is stock and final line restates rather than snaps.
Exact two seeds and some absurd escalation, but no sharp final laugh line.
Three seed concepts; mild discovery punch, competent but thin.
Solid premise and a clean final turn; familiar but effective.
Clear escalation and first‑person rhythm; the ending lands mildly.

Clean and coherent but more predictable; a competent light joke.
